messages:
cs-jordan: Customer report — multiple 503s in the last 15m from acme-prod. Ticket C-8921. They see gateway 503s and timeouts for text-generation and tool calls (~10-20s) then 503. Trying to reproduce but hitting infra limits. Sample curl response attached in ticket.

alex: can you paste runner logs + dmesg? Any model swap/hotswap happening around the time?

cs-jordan: excerpts from customer attached logs and kernel snippet:
```
[runner] 2026-03-16T21:12:45Z ERROR infer-runner: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f12a3b4 pc 0x7f12a3b4
kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 3245 (infer-runner) total-vm:204800kB, anon-rss:180000kB
nvml: GPU 0: out of memory while allocating 1.2 GiB
```

maya: that nvml line + segfault pattern looks like GPU OOM during KV prefetch. Did they enable quantized hotswap or new batching tweak in last deploy?

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-16T20:58:12 — team/eng-runtime — rolled out model-prefetch-batching v2.3 to hosted cluster (rolling).

alex: repro hypothesis: high sustained QPS + long context windows + autotuned batch_size -> memory spike, followed by segfault on memory allocation path. Need core + nvprof to be sure.

eng-oncall: triage notes: container infer-3245 on host ip 10.4.9.21 restarted 6x between 20:58 and 21:14. coredump present at /var/crash/infer-3245.core. dmesg shows oom_kill targeting infer-runner. Marking P1 — multi-customer impact due to 503s.

sophie: immediate mitigations:
- fallback route traffic to smaller model variant (reduce mem footprint)
- pin affected customers to Dedicated capacity where possible
- rollback the batching/prefetch change if confirmed causality
I'll open canary rollback and enable fallback routing.

ops-bot: Host 10.4.9.21: container infer-3245 restart count=6 in 16m. GPU0 mem at crash=100%, GPU util=98%.

alex: attempted repro on staging: context_len=2048, batch_size=16, kv-prefetch=on -> reproduced segfault within ~30s. Temp mitigation on staging: set max_batch_size=8 and disable kv-prefetch; stable afterwards.

cs-jordan: CS message to customer: "We see upstream inference workers crashing due to GPU memory spikes; temporary mitigations are available (reduced batch_size or pinning to Dedicated). We're prioritizing a rollback and patch. Will update within 60 minutes." Customer asked about billing and SLA credit.

billing-bot: Note: any pinning to Dedicated or capacity change requires sales approval; short-term quota bump can be approved by Ops for incident mitigation. Billing impact to be assessed after resolution.

eng-oncall: next steps checklist:
1) collect full coredump + nvprof + dmesg (@maya)
2) open rollback PR for model-prefetch-batching v2.3 (@alex)
3) enable fallback routing and canary to smaller model (@sophie)
4) coordinate a CS update cadence (@cs-jordan)
Assigning owners: @alex (rollback PR + test), @maya (upload traces), @sophie (fallback + routing), @cs-jordan (customer comms).

alex: opening PR now and will attach a deterministic repro test case run against staging.

maya: uploading core + nvml traces to /mnt/triage/1749302468/ (core, nvprof, dmesg.txt). Also attaching exact command used to reproduce:
```
python tools/loadtest.py --qps 120 --context 2048 --batch-autotune=true --kv-prefetch
```

sophie: enabling fallback routing for acme-prod to model-small-v1 and throttling batch autoscale for the next 30m. Will monitor.

cs-jordan: sent customer update: "Mitigation applied (fallback + temporary batch cap). Investigating root cause; will provide timeline for fix." Customer acknowledged, asks for ETA on rollback.

eng-oncall: ETA: rollback canary in 10m, full rollback if canary stable in 30m. Logging follow-ups here. :thumbsup:

alex: PR opened: revert model-prefetch-batching v2.3 (link: https://git/repo/pull/4321) — includes config to disable kv-prefetch by default.

maya: core and nvml traces uploaded. Grep of coredump shows crash in attention kernel allocation path; will follow up with kernel devs if needed.

cs-jordan: keeping the ticket open and will update if customer asks for credits. Thanks all."
